- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.7) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects; reduce subsequent forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true price deviates from recent 7-day average by >3%, model shows lag; adjust forecast to align with 7-day moving average if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.5), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 periods unless sentiment confirms trend.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply downward bias of 1–2% for first 5–7 periods if sentiment is weak or mixed.
